evidence: Both candidates honour the Silkscreen Jasmine Corolla concept: flat gentian field, matte mint八-lobed scalloped corolla passing behind the flacon's shoulders as a graphic halo, shadowless frontal ink light, faithful opaque mint body with ribbed gold cap and legible Flora label, and a sans typographic plaque in the lower band with the poppy registration rule. Version 2 (image 6) resolves the plaque better: the short poppy rule floats with clear air between the corolla's bottom lobe tip and the tracked GUCCI brand line, and the rule-brand-name stack is evenly spaced inside a calm lower band, giving cleaner hierarchy and a true registration-mark read. Version 1 (image 5) crowds the rule against the corolla's lower point and pushes the name line higher, leaving a dead empty strip at the foot of the poster; its plaque feels compressed rather than calm. Version 2's centred name line sits better balanced within the band width while keeping the wide tracking and geometric sans family.
remaining_problems: The corolla's lower lobe tip protrudes below the bottle base as a small stray point that still visually nudges the poppy rule zone in both versions; trimming or masking it behind the base would clean the silhouette.
The name line, though wide, sits slightly closer to the poster's bottom edge than to the brand line in version 2, leaving the lower band marginally bottom-heavy.
The corolla reads as four visible side lobes plus hidden top/bottom lobes behind the flacon; the eight-lobed scallop count is only partly legible at poster scale.
